validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real. American Midstream announced an open season Feb 22, 2016 to extend the existing Magnolia Intrastate Pipeline system with a new ~45-mile segment connecting into Tennessee Gas Pipeline's 500 Line and the Transco system near the MS/AL border, targeting a 2019 in-service date (Business Wire release, restated by Oil & Gas Journal -- ogj.com/pipelines/article -- same underlying announcement, one origin). EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects workbook independently and continuously tracks this project (Operator 'American Midstream', $45M cost, 500 MMcf/d capacity, MS->AL) from its 2018 release through the current 2026-08 release, first as 'Announced' then (from the 2019-10 release onward, last_updated_date 2019-08-14) as 'On Hold' -- a second, independent, federal-statistical-agency origin distinct from the operator's own press release. CLASSIFICATION: reasonable as an interstate-connecting transmission-type extension (it is described as a new pipeline segment linking two existing mainline systems -- TGP 500 Line and Transco -- for the purpose of moving gas to new markets, not as a well/wellpad gathering line); no source explicitly labels it 'transmission' but nothing supports 'gathering' or 'distribution' either, and EIA's own Pipeline Type field for this project is blank in the workbook. DUPLICATE: not a duplicate. Confirmed distinct from (a) the EXISTING Magnolia System itself (~118 miles of coal-bed-methane gathering/trunk lines in 5 Alabama counties, Section 311 intrastate, per American Midstream Partners' FY2016 10-K, SEC EDGAR CIK 1513965) -- that is the parent system this row's 'Extension' proposes to extend, a different (larger, already-built) asset, and (b) P2559 'Magnolia Gas Pipeline' -- a separate, larger EIA-tracked project ($202M cost, 1,362 MMcf/d capacity) confirmed via the EIA long-format history CSV to be a distinct project_key with different cost/capacity figures throughout its own release history. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1 'Third Coast Midstream LLC' is independently confirmed via SEC EDGAR's own company-facts index (data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001513965.json), which documents CIK 1513965's name change from 'American Midstream Partners, LP' to 'Third Coast Midstream, LLC' effective 2019-07-19 -- the same corporate lineage named in the 2016 announcement, now under its current legal name. One caveat carried into the fills below: several of this row's data points (Proposal date, Start year, Length) trace to a single underlying document (the Feb 2016 open-season announcement, restated once by OGJ) rather than to two fully independent origins, so those individual fills are tiered medium rather than high even though overall existence is well corroborated by the independent EIA thread. [Repoint note: the EIA citation above was repointed from the undated workbook to the Aug2026 dated release, sheet 'Historical Projects (1996-2024)', Excel row 1157, confirming the project is still tracked (Status = On Hold) as of the current release; the 2019 Announced->On Hold transition referenced in this note is separately dated to the Oct2019 release (sheet 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects', Excel row 84) in the Status/Shelved fills below.]

status_reviews.researcher_notes: The sheet's Status=shelved traces to EIA's own status transition (Announced -> On Hold) dated 2019-08-14 per the EIA long-format project history. EIA itself has carried the project as 'On Hold' continuously through its most recent 2026-08 release without ever marking it cancelled, but with NO substantive update to the underlying record since 2019-08-14 -- i.e., 7 years of dormancy on the last actual dated evidence. Tested for revival before recommending: searched for any post-2019 news of construction, FID, open-season renewal, or formal cancellation (none found via OGJ, general web search, or SEC EDGAR full-text search of Third Coast Midstream's own filings); checked Third Coast Midstream's current public asset/system descriptions (third-coast.com and its predecessor pages) for any current mention of a Magnolia extension/expansion project (none found; the current asset list does not include this project among active or planned systems); no FERC docket exists to check (Section 311 intrastate, state-authority project per EIA's Authority field), and Alabama/Mississippi PSC docket search interfaces were not accessible as static/queryable pages in this session. Per the sweep's dormancy rule, 7 years shelved with no independent revival evidence exceeds the 4-year shelved->cancelled threshold, warranting a 'stale' verdict with a recommended change to Status=cancelled, ShelvedCancelledType=inferred. No ref is proposed for the inference itself (proposed_refs intentionally empty here), per the standing rule against fabricating a URL for an inferred dormancy-based status change; the evidence_date (2019-08) is EIA's last actual dated update, cited above in the Status/Shelved fills. | ORCHESTRATOR 2026-09-14: tier demoted to low and independent -> false. Rule 4 sets `high`/independent at 2+ INDEPENDENT origins; this record's verified refs resolve to 0 publisher(s) (none verified). No ref passed ok+contains_value, so nothing is verified-corroborated.
